title: Sean Dyche on Forest future: ‘If the owner wants to make a change, that’s up to him’
content:
Sean Dyche says it is up to Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis whether he wants to make a change in the dugout.

The 54-year-old had been under pressure coming into Forest’s clash with Wolverhampton Wanderers on Wednesday and, while they dominated the game — mustering 35 shots — they were held to a 0-0 draw at the City Ground.

Dyche says he is working hard to get Forest moving in the right direction, but the former Forest academy player said it is down to Marinakis to decide on his future.

If the Greek shipping magnate did decide to swing the axe, it would mean a fourth head coach in the space of one season for Forest.

Nuno Espirito Santo departed in September, Ange Postecoglou lasted 39 days and Dyche has been in charge since October.

“The owner has been fair to me, without a shadow of a doubt. Fair on the situation,” said Dyche in his post-match press conference. “If anyone wants to change in football now, that’s their decision.

“People can demand change, and then it’s always up to owners whether they change or not.

“I just work very hard. I care about this club. I’ve made that clear. I’m working very hard. I’m not saying the players are not, by the way, but we certainly are as a staff, that’s what you do. You know, we work very hard.

“If the owner wants to make a change, then that’s up to him, and that’s the way football is now, that’s just the reality of it.

“But I’m not questioning the owner here. He’s been absolutely fair with me from the beginning to the end, and I’ve been fair with him and told him the truth every step of the way.”

When asked if he expected a change, Dyche said: “What I’m saying is owners are owners. They don’t warm you up, it just comes and it comes, if that’s the way it goes.

“I’m a realist. I understand, you know, the noise here has changed significantly since the last few games.

“I’m frustrated as it’s (been) not a terrible run. But that’s still the modern way football is. Demand is high. That’s changed enormously in the last probably two years. Demand is getting higher and higher and higher and higher.”

Forest had been unbeaten in four games prior to a painful 3-1 defeat at Leeds United and tonight’s 0-0 draw with Wolves.

But poor performances against Everton — both home and away — in Braga and against Wrexham in the FA Cup have been hanging over Dyche.
